title: "Functions"
format: html

This script defines the helper functions that export and summarize tables. None of them changes an estimate. They are new in the repository version: the original R Markdown file printed its results inline, and scripts run with `source()` need to save them instead.

::: {.Rcode title="Source code"}
The full R script is available at:

-   [`R/functions.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Pirofski-cryptococcus-study/blob/master/R/functions.R)

This R script file is itself reliant on the following helper files:

-   [`R/setup.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Pirofski-cryptococcus-study/blob/master/R/setup.R)

The code sections below are imported directly from that script when this page is rendered.
:::

```{r}
#| include: false
#| eval: true
#| cache: false
knitr::read_chunk("../R/functions.R")
```

## Save a gtsummary table

Converts any `gtsummary` table (Table 1, regression and merged tables) to a `gt` table and saves it as a self-contained HTML file. Used by [Tables](tables.qmd).

```{r}
#| label: save-gtsummary-html
#| eval: false
```

## Relabel a table for display

Replaces variable names and category codes in a gtsummary table with the readable labels defined in [Setup](setup.qmd), by editing only the table's label column. Estimates, confidence intervals, p-values, reference categories and row order are unchanged; variables or categories without a display label are left as they are. Used by [Tables](tables.qmd) just before each gtsummary table is saved.

```{r}
#| label: relabel-table
#| eval: false
```

## Save a data frame as a table

Formats a data frame with `flextable` and saves it as HTML. Used for the AUC confidence intervals and optimal cutpoints.

```{r}
#| label: save-flextable-html
#| eval: false
```

## Summarize an optimal cutpoint

Takes one `cutpointr` result from [Regression, ROC and cutpoints](modeling.qmd) and returns one row: the optimal cutpoint and its sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive value, and AUC. Nothing is recomputed; the values are read from the `cutpointr` object.

```{r}
#| label: summarise-cutpoint
#| eval: false
```

## Summarize AUC confidence intervals

Takes the DeLong and bootstrap results of `pROC::ci.auc()` for one ROC curve and returns one row with the AUC and both 95% confidence intervals. `ci.auc()` returns the lower limit, the AUC and the upper limit, in that order.

```{r}
#| label: summarise-auc-ci
#| eval: false
```
